summary: Every visitor to South Sudan needs a visa: most nationalities apply online through the official eVisa portal (evisa.gov.ss) or at an embassy. No official visa fee is currently published. The UK, Canadian and Australian governments advise against all travel to South Sudan.

UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — South Sudan travel advice: entry requirements

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in South Sudan.

source.name: UK FCDO travel advice — South Sudan entry requirements

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required of all travellers aged 9 months or over, whatever country you arrive from. South Sudan itself has yellow fever risk.

source.name: WHO — Vaccination requirements and recommendations for international travellers, country list (ITH 2022)

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: Malaria transmission is intense year-round throughout South Sudan. Antimalarial tablets, repellent and bed nets are strongly recommended — talk to a travel clinic before your trip.

source.name: WHO — Vaccination requirements and recommendations for international travellers, country list (ITH 2022)

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for South Sudan. The UK Foreign Office says health facilities are extremely limited throughout the country and many medical problems need evacuation to Nairobi or Kampala, and advises adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds for treatment, evacuation and repatriation.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — South Sudan travel advice: health

onwardTicket.text: No official source we could read states an onward- or return-ticket requirement for South Sudan.

source.name: South Sudan eVisa portal — Directorate of Nationality, Passports and Immigration

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could read states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount for South Sudan.

source.name: South Sudan eVisa portal — Directorate of Nationality, Passports and Immigration

declarations.name: Registration with the police
declarations.text: If you stay in South Sudan for 5 days or more, you must register at a local police station.

source.name: UK FCDO travel advice — South Sudan entry requirements

currencyLimits.text: No official source we could read states South Sudan's cash-declaration threshold. The UK Foreign Office says you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty, and to ask the South Sudanese Embassy for the rules.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — South Sudan travel advice: entry requirements

notes: The UK Foreign Office says there are strict rules on goods you can take into or out of South Sudan, and you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

Canada's travel advice says a permit from the Ministry of Information is required for photography, including on a mobile phone, and that even with one it is prohibited to photograph military installations, military and police personnel, government buildings and infrastructure such as roads, bridges, dams and airfields, and public utilities.

payments.text: The UK Foreign Office says international cards are not widely accepted, though some newer hotels and supermarkets are starting to, and ATMs are hard to find and often do not take international cards; it advises bringing large-denomination US dollars in clean, unmarked notes dated 2017 or later. Canada's travel advice says larger expenses such as hotel bills must be paid in cash, and that changing money outside banks and exchange bureaus is illegal.

safety.text: The UK, Canadian and Australian governments advise against all travel to South Sudan. The UK cites the risk of armed violence and criminality; Canada cites armed conflict, inter-ethnic violence, high levels of violent crime and a risk of kidnapping. The UK says the security situation could deteriorate rapidly and unpredictably.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — South Sudan travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit South Sudan. The UK Foreign Office says that during the rainy season, from April to November, most roads outside Juba become impassable and there is a risk of being cut off by floods.

emergency.name: Government of Canada — South Sudan travel advice: emergency assistance

conflict.name: Australian Government Smartraveller — South Sudan travel advice: local emergency contacts
conflict.states: fire and rescue 999, medical emergencies 999, police 999 or 777

languages.name: UK Permanent Committee on Geographical Names (FCDO) — South Sudan toponymic factfile: languages

currency.name: Government of Canada — South Sudan travel advice: laws and culture: money

payments.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — South Sudan travel advice: safety and security: money

bestTimeToVisit.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — South Sudan travel advice: safety and security: extreme weather

tapWaterSafe.name: Australian Government Smartraveller — South Sudan travel advice (Health: "Drink only boiled or bottled water")

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to South Sudan because of the risk of armed violence and criminality, and Canada says to avoid all travel. Canada warns of a risk of kidnapping, particularly in isolated areas.

Canada's travel advice says photography, even on a phone, requires a permit from the Ministry of Information, and that even with a permit you may not photograph military installations, police or military personnel, government buildings, roads, bridges, dams, airfields or public utilities.
The UK Foreign Office says you must register at a local police station if you are in South Sudan for 5 days or more.

The UK Foreign Office advises bringing large-denomination US dollars in clean, unblemished notes dated 2017 or later, as marked notes are likely to be refused; Canada says notes dated before 2006 are not accepted. Australia's Smartraveller recommends carrying enough US dollars to cover your whole stay.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for South Sudan?
faq.answer: Yes — every nationality needs a visa for South Sudan. Most travelers apply online through the official eVisa portal at evisa.gov.ss or at a South Sudanese embassy before travel.

faq.question: Is there a visa on arrival in South Sudan?
faq.answer: Not reliably — airlines generally require an eVisa approval or embassy visa before boarding flights to Juba. Apply online in advance rather than counting on arrangements at the airport.

faq.question: Is South Sudan safe to visit?
faq.answer: No. The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to South Sudan because of the risk of armed violence and criminality, and Canada says to avoid all travel because of the volatile security situation, armed conflict, inter-ethnic violence and high levels of violent crime.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for South Sudan?
faq.answer: Yes. The WHO country list states that proof of yellow fever vaccination is required of all travellers aged 9 months or over, whatever country they arrive from, and the UK FCDO also lists the certificate as an entry requirement.

faq.question: Can I use the South Sudan eVisa at land borders?
faq.answer: The eVisa is designed around arrival at Juba International Airport. Land-border handling is inconsistent — if you must cross overland, get a visa from an embassy beforehand and confirm the crossing is open and considered passable.
